purpose: Maps an annotated VCF's INFO fields onto evidence fields for acmg_pipeline.providers.vcf_annotation. Which field means what is a property of the annotator that wrote the file, so this MUST be checked against a real header from the annotator actually in use before it is applied. Nothing here has been validated against an operational file.
limitations: The VEP entry is derived from VEP's documented CSQ layout, not from an output file this project has seen. VEP's field set depends on which plugins and --fields were used, so the subfield names present in a real header may differ.

The bcftools entry assumes gnomAD-prefixed field names from `bcftools annotate -a gnomad.vcf.gz -c INFO/gnomAD_AF,...`. The names are whatever the -c argument assigned, so they are installation-specific.
Both are starting points for reading a real header, not defaults to apply unseen.
Fields a curator already concluded (CLNSIG, ACMG_CODES and the rest of providers.vcf_annotation.REFUSED) cannot appear here; the provider raises if they do.

The cross-gene-annotation-explorer entry is the one checked against a real file (selected_variants_2026-09-14testyuko.vcf, 44 variants). Its version_declaration is a stated assumption, not something the file says - see the note on that entry.

ensembl-vep-vcf.note: `vep --vcf` packs every subfield into CSQ and declares the order in the ##INFO header's Format clause. The provider reads that clause, so the order below is not relied on - only the names are. One entry per transcript is present; only the entry matching the transcript being evaluated is read.

snpeff-vcf.note: SnpEff's ANN field has the same shape with different subfield names, declared as "Functional annotations: 'Allele | Annotation | ...'". Included to show the second shape the provider handles; the field list is illustrative.

bcftools-annotate-gnomad.note: Flat one-field-per-value output. Fields sharing a `group` become one evidence record, so AF, AC and AN arrive together as a single population observation. `callable` is not derivable from these fields and is deliberately absent - usable_observations() requires it for an AC of 0, so an absent variant still cannot be read as AF 0.

cross-gene-annotation-explorer.note: VEP output flattened into VEP_* fields rather than a CSQ block, so the flat shape applies. The file names no fileDate, no reference, and no Source or Version on any INFO line - it says only that it used VEP - so without the declaration below nothing in it can be pinned and every field is skipped.

version_declaration.justification: The exporter reports that it annotated with VEP and gnomAD but names no release in the file, so the releases are declared here instead. gnomAD 4.1.1 is not a guess: the GNOMAD_AF of four variants was compared against the gnomAD 4.1.1 API and matched its exome global allele frequency to six significant figures (CHRNA1 2-174757593-C-T 1.094500e-05, MBD4 3-129437103-G-A 1.094720e-05, IDUA 4-1001742-T-C 1.589390e-05, OSGEP 14-20449182-G-A 1.851240e-05); the genome frequencies of the same release differ, so the field is the exome subset specifically. The VEP release is still unconfirmed - consequence terms are stable across releases, so the file's own values cannot date it - and must come from the exporter's configuration. Every record built under this declaration carries version_status=DECLARED with this text, so a curator can see which version was verified and which was asserted.

undeclared.Ensembl VEP: Unconfirmed. Left out of declared_versions on purpose rather than left as a placeholder, because a placeholder string would satisfy the declaration and pass as a version. While it is absent, VEP_* fields stay unpinned and the Ensembl provider fetches the annotation instead. Add it once the exporter's configured release is known.
undeclared.dbNSFP: Never stated by the file and not verifiable from it.

not_usable_from_this_file.population: GNOMAD_AF is gnomAD 4.1.1's exome global frequency (verified, see the declaration) but arrives with no AC or AN, and usable_observations() needs both - so PM2, BA1 and BS1 cannot run on it, and BS1's filtering allele frequency cannot be computed either. An AF of 0 also cannot be read as absence, because nothing in the file states callability. GNOMAD_AF_GRPMAX is a second statistic over the same release rather than a population observation of its own, so it is mapped to its own field rather than joining the AF record as though it were one.
not_usable_from_this_file.transcript: VEP_TRANSCRIPT holds an Ensembl accession (ENST...) while the pipeline evaluates RefSeq (NM_...). The MANE summary carries both, so a translation step is possible, but none exists yet.
not_usable_from_this_file.AM_CLASS: A classification with no score, and computational.py scores against calibrated intervals.
not_usable_from_this_file.biotype: Some rows are annotated on retained_intron or nonsense_mediated_decay transcripts, which may not be the transcript to evaluate.
not_usable_from_this_file.assembly: No ##reference and no ASSEMBLY in INFO. Without an assembly passed in, all 44 rows fail as INVALID_VARIANT and none reaches the pipeline. See declared_assembly.

declared_assembly.justification: The file states no ##reference and carries no ASSEMBLY in INFO, so audit_vcf() rejects every row with INVALID_VARIANT - the same coordinates mean different variants on GRCh37 and GRCh38, and guessing is not detectable after the fact. GRCh38 is not a guess here: the file's GNOMAD_AF matched gnomAD 4.1.1, which is GRCh38-only, to six significant figures on four variants (see version_declaration). Pass it as audit_vcf(path, assembly="GRCh38"). The declaration is not visible in the row itself - a declared build looks exactly like a read one - so it is legible only here and in the run manifest, and it applies only to files matching applies_when. A file that does state its own ##reference stays the authority: audit_vcf keeps the row and marks it ASSEMBLY_CONFLICT rather than letting the declaration overwrite it.
declared_assembly.applies_when: The file's ##source matches version_declaration.matches_source and it states no ##reference of its own.
